subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on or opt-in two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity source, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, parent wake behavior, and channel-visible notification should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds public config/default behavior, automatic child-run mutation, parent queue unblocking, and user-visible channel semantics that source evidence cannot safely choose for maintainers.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt the feature after maintainers specify defaults or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and false-positive protections.

options.title: Prototype default-off watchdog
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in implementation first, with focused live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until maintainers accept defaults.

options.title: Defer automatic recovery
options.body: Rely on runTimeoutSeconds, diagnostics recovery, and future manual kill/reap controls until more production evidence or a broader session activity contract lands.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature after maintainers specify defaults or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and false-positive protections.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest current-main history across the subagent registry/control boundary and adjacent timeout semantics that the policy would extend.
